chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Harun ibn Harijah, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I deposit money in the treasury (bayt al-mal) on the condition that I take six [dirhams] from every thousand [as a fee/administration cost].' He said, 'The calculation of the reward/fee is for the one who receives it (the agent/administrator).'

key_terms.بَيْتُ الْمَالِ: The public treasury or state fund
key_terms.لِلْآجِرِ: For the agent/one who receives the wage

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on deducting an administrative fee from public funds in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Harun ibn Harijah inquired of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the permissibility of deducting a six-dirham administrative fee per thousand when depositing funds into the public treasury. The Imam affirmed this practice with the principle that 'the calculation of the reward belongs to the agent,' establishing the legal basis for *ujrah* (service fee) in financial administration. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly view that compensation for managing public or private assets is a legitimate right of the administrator, provided it is agreed upon.
